strategy.summary: Reproduce the SciPy sparse LaplacianNd periodic eigenvectors correctness bug by running the project test that reconstructs the Laplacian from eigenvectors. Build SciPy at the buggy commit (04b8f858c947), run the specific pytest test; it should fail via the new full eigendecomposition/orthogonality assertions for grid_shape=(6,) and boundary_conditions="periodic". Then switch to the fixed revision (the PR’s post-fix commit) and confirm the same test passes.

build_commands: python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
pinned_because: No version constraints are provided in the evidence. The strategy selects a single explicit SciPy source revision (the buggy commit) and relies on compatible NumPy/pytest installed from PyPI; if the failure is version-sensitive, you may need to pin NumPy/pytest to match the CI environment that observed the bug.

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest -q scipy/sparse/linalg/tests/test_special_sparse_arrays.py -k "test_eigenvectors and bc==periodic and grid_shape==6"
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy SciPy revision (commit 04b8f858c947) the added assertions in test_eigenvectors fail for grid_shape=(6,) and bc='periodic': either (1) assert_allclose(eigenvectors @ eigenvectors.T, np.eye(n), atol=atol) fails due to incorrect/duplicate eigenvectors, or (2) assert_allclose(L, lap.toarray(), atol=atol) fails where L = eigenvectors @ diag(eigenvalues) @ eigenvectors.T. On the fixed revision of the PR the same parametrization passes (no AssertionError).
strategy.numerical_probe: Construct lap = LaplacianNd(grid_shape=(6,), boundary_conditions="periodic"); compute eigenvectors = lap.eigenvectors(m) and eigenvalues = lap.eigenvalues(m) for the test’s chosen m values, then verify L = eigenvectors @ diag(eigenvalues) @ eigenvectors.T matches lap.toarray(). The failure is due to incorrect eigenvector construction (duplicate eigenvectors) in the periodic case for one parity branch.

input_output_examples.input: n=6; grid_shape=(6,); lap = scipy.sparse.linalg.LaplacianNd(grid_shape, boundary_conditions="periodic"); evaluate the test’s reconstruction: L = lap.eigenvectors(m) @ np.diag(lap.eigenvalues()) @ lap.eigenvectors(m).T and compare to lap.toarray() using np.allclose within atol
input_output_examples.expected_output: No AssertionError; the equality check succeeds within atol

risks: No explicit NumPy/SciPy version constraints were provided (both are unbounded in the evidence). If the bug is sensitive to specific NumPy linear algebra backends or BLAS/LAPACK versions, you may need to pin NumPy (and/or SciPy build options) to the versions used when the bug was observed.
The evidence does not state which fixed commit to use; you must check out the PR’s post-fix revision (e.g., merge commit or the commit after 04b8f858c947) so that test_eigenvectors passes.

The exact pytest selector in test_command uses parameter values in the -k expression; depending on pytest collection naming, you may need to run the whole test file with -k test_eigenvectors and then identify the failing parameter set (grid_shape=(6,), bc='periodic').

If the failure only reproduces on a specific platform/architecture (e.g., due to floating-point behavior), it may not transition across all environments. Run at least on Linux x86_64 with default SciPy build settings unless you know the original environment.

oracle.reference_source: Project test oracle: np.testing.assert_allclose via the SciPy test added/modified in PR#23121. It checks orthogonality eigenvectors @ eigenvectors.T ≈ I and full reconstruction eigenvectors @ diag(eigenvalues) @ eigenvectors.T ≈ lap.toarray(), both within atol used by the test.
oracle.why: The correctness bug is defined by failing the test’s internal allclose assertions, not by inspecting individual eigenvector values.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The new assertions in test_eigenvectors fail for grid_shape=(6,) and boundary_conditions='periodic' on commit 04b8f858c947, because lap.eigenvectors() contains incorrect/duplicate eigenvectors so that either the orthogonality check or the full reconstruction check raises AssertionError when using assert_allclose.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision corresponding to PR#23121 after the eigenvector construction change is corrected, the same parametrized test (grid_shape=(6,), bc='periodic') passes with no AssertionError.
